items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went on Broadway in 1931 with Dave Nelson. I played Mae West’s show... Dave Nelson had a band.

ctx.x: Because of the money. That’s why. Money first. Work every week. Two jobs. Work the Cotton Club and play in the theater in daytime. Play the Paramount, the Grand, and the Lowes. You play them theaters in Brooklyn. You can play about six weeks around New York The Bronx has a couple of theaters. Brooklyn. Yonkers. Queens. All them theaters. People, loaded with people. Theaters. You play that. Cab Calloway was doing all that. He had a band. He had [Albert] Socarras’s band, a great Cuban flute player. He had…

club some black people opened. Hell of a club. The people didn’t know too much about show business. They had the place loaded with booze. Big trucks loaded with booze used to come in. They didn’t sell that kind of booze, but the band drank up all the booze. You had the bands right in front of the bandstand. Everybody had him a quart. The bartenders didn’t say nothing. They just ripped the people off. Club closed. Different bands. Dave Nelson had a band. That was King Oliver’s nephew. I went on Broadway in 1931…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Dave Nelson got the job in a cabaret scene, and using a five-piece band. So we... I'm on Broadway!

ctx.x: Yeah. You look at the picture with Dave Nelson and...who else was in that picture... Out of Chicago? She got on diamonds. That was the current thing, you know what I mean?

So when you played the Eighty-One Theatre, man, you had to be, like, you know, good, or you didn't make more than one show. So the Eighty-One Theatre and the theatre in Baltimore, and there was one in Memphis... Man, there must have been about fifteen cities. Birmingham, Alabama. Mobile...

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: we're in this band, Dave Nelson's band... [INTERVIEWER] Pianist. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. So we get to be tight

ctx.x: A drummer who worked with Fats Waller. And Slick Jones wife was a nice performer. Can't think of her name now. Well, we're in this band, Dave Nelson's band. Lawrence Phillips is in this band, too.
Yeah. So we get to be tight, and I'm beginning to understand what great piano playing is all about.
